text:
alex: Heads up — planned rolling maintenance for GPU inference fleet in us-west-2 on Sat 2024-06-15 02:00-05:00 UTC. Rebooting nodes to apply kernel + driver security patches. Goal is zero customer-impact but expect short cold-starts and brief capacity dips.

maya: Plan sketch: drain 4 nodes at a time, 15m staggers. Autoscaler bump to +20% spare capacity during window. Canary first (single node from tenant-pool-a) then full roll.

jonathan: Quick question — this only targets inference pools (g4dn/g5-like) and not the training clusters, right?

alex: Correct, only inference pools. Training clusters unaffected.

lina: @sre-oncall can you own pager during the window? We'll also need a scheduled incident on the status page and a customer note.

sre-oncall: I got this. I'll create the scheduled maintenance incident at start time, attach the runbook, and enable infra escalations. Link to runbook: https://internal/runbooks/gpu-reboot 

infra-bot: Ops hint — use: `kubectl cordon <node>` then `kubectl drain <node> --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=120` . After reboot ensure `nvidia-smi` shows GPUs and `kubectl wait --for=condition=Ready node/<node>`.

maya: Ops steps TL;DR:
1) cordon node
2) drain pods (evict + wait)
3) reboot node
4) verify driver + kube ready
5) uncordon
I'll push the helper script to #eng-infra later today.

jonathan: Concern: some models have 2–4s cold-starts and p95 could spike if too many nodes are drained concurrently. Suggest pre-warm: after pods come up, send synthetic requests to warm caches (10 requests per model).

alex: Good call — we'll route 10% canary traffic for 10m to validate before continuing each batch.

maya: Cost question: the autoscaler bump adds ~10% extra GPU-hours for the window. @sam-finance ok?

sam-finance: Budget approved for the safety margin. Keep estimate <30 total extra GPU-hours and flag if we exceed.

lina: I'll prepare a short customer-facing blurb: "Scheduled maintenance in us-west-2 may cause brief latency increases as we rotate capacity; no expected downtime." Will post to customers 24h and 1h prior.

alex: Node batches (rough): batch A: node-uw2-01..04, batch B: 05..08, batch C: 09..12. We'll adjust if pod pressure is high.

maya: Small nit: set HPA minReplicas to avoid scale-to-zero during window for critical services. Also set pod disruption budgets for high-traffic model deployments to 1.

jonathan: I'll coordinate with model infra owners to ensure critical deployments have PDBs and readiness probes tuned.

infra-bot: Reminder: enable rolling reboot label `maintenance/2024-06-15=yes` so we can filter nodes in dashboard.

lina: I'll post update in #customer-success and #support once maintenance ticket is created.

alex: Timeline recap: Sat 2024-06-15 02:00 UTC start, 3-hour window, 4-node batches every 15m, canary then full. Objective: patch + reboot + verify without hitting SLOs.

maya: I'll run the first canary at 02:05 and report results here. :eyes:

jonathan: Pre-warm script ready, will run after each node recovers.

sre-oncall: Pager coverage confirmed. I'll escalate on failures after 2 failed batches.

sam-finance: :thumbsup: keep me posted if anything extends beyond window.

alex: Thanks all — post any blockers now otherwise proceed with the timeline.

maya: ACK.

jonathan: ACK.

lina: ACK.

infra-bot: Scheduled maintenance event created and pinned to channel.
